question.prompt: The sum of two numbers is 20, and their difference is 6. Find the two numbers. (Write the larger number first, followed by the smaller number, separated by a comma.)

solutions.explanation: Let the larger number be \(x\) and the smaller number be \(y\): \(x+y=20\), \(x-y=6\). Adding gives \(2x=26\), so \(x=13\), \(y=7\).
solutions.title: Model the sum and difference

solutions.explanation:
Subtracting \(6\) from the larger number makes it equal to the smaller number. Their total is now \(20-6\), made up of two copies of the smaller number. Thus the smaller number is
\[
(20-6)\div2=7.
\]
Adding back the difference gives the larger number, \(7+6=13\). The answer is \(13,7\).
solutions.title: Equalize the numbers
